title: Open restriction and rigidity of supplied relative dualizing pairs over arbitrary bases
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a separated flat locally finitely presented morphism of arbitrary schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose $(K,\xi)$ and $(L,\eta)$ are supplied coherent relative dualizing pairs [def-trf-coherent-relative-dualizing-pair], with diagonal $\Delta:X\to X\times_SX$ and first projection $p_1$. For every open $U\subset X$, their restrictions are coherent relative dualizing pairs for $U/S$. The scalar map $\mathcal O_X\to R\mathcal Hom_X(K,K)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. There is exactly one isomorphism $\alpha:K\to L$ satisfying $(Lp_1^*\alpha)\xi=\eta$ [def-pc-derived-pullback]. These assertions hold after every open restriction, including the empty open. If $V\subset S$ is open and $f$ factors through $V$, the same pairs and comparisons are obtained using $X/V$ instead of $X/S$. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For an open $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ put $Y_U=U\times_SU\subset Y$; $\Delta^{-1}(Y_U)=U$ and the restricted closed subscheme is the diagonal of $U/S$, so $f|_U$ is separated. It is flat (same stalk maps) and locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] on affine charts inside $U$. On an open $H\subset Y_U$, $(\Delta_*\mathcal O_X)(H)=\mathcal O_X(\Delta^{-1}H)=\mathcal O_U(\Delta_U^{-1}H)$, identifying the restricted diagonal algebra with $\Delta_{U*}\mathcal O_U$, with its product and unit. Since $p_1|_{Y_U}=j\circ p_{1,U}$, [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde](1) gives $(Lp_1^*K)|_{Y_U}\cong Lp_{1,U}^*(K|_U)$ (defining $\xi_U$) and restriction comparisons $m_0$ for derived tensors. On a K-flat $P$ (restriction keeps it K-flat by [lem-sfb-ringed-site-restriction-kflat]) and any $N$, $m_0$ is induced by the termwise equality $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes N)|_{Y_U}=\operatorname{Tot}(P|_{Y_U}\otimes N|_{Y_U})$, so it is strong monoidal and carries the localization map $\mu_Y$ of [def-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-comparison] to $\mu_{Y_U}$; hence it carries the derived multiplication of $\Delta_*\mathcal O_X$ to that of $\Delta_{U*}\mathcal O_U$. Let $r$ be restriction and $c=e_U^{-1}(\mu_{m_0};r(e(1)))$; it is an isomorphism by [lem-pc-open-restriction-evaluation-mate-is-iso], and naturality of the tensor--Hom bijections [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection] gives $e_U(r\varphi;c)=\mu_{m_0};r(e\varphi)$ for every $\varphi$. Applied to multiplication by $\xi$, this gives $c\circ r(m_\xi)=m_{\xi_U}$, an isomorphism. Pseudo-coherence restricts by restricting the local finite-free models. For finite Tor amplitude, on an amplitude neighbourhood $T$ extend a test $(f^{-1}\mathcal O_S)|_{T\cap U}$-module by zero; restriction is exact and keeps K-flatness [lem-sfb-ringed-site-restriction-kflat], so restricting the tensor gives the test tensor and the bound persists. So $K|_U,L|_U$ satisfy the supplied-pair predicate.

source.place: Tag 0E2X, open-restriction observation; Tag 0E2T, supplied-pair conditions.

proof.text: Take the basis $\mathcal B$ of affine opens of $X$ mapping into affine opens of $S$; around any point of any open one first chooses an affine target neighbourhood and then an affine source neighbourhood inside its inverse image. For $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ over $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, the affine-realization node gives $M,N$, the classes $\gamma,\theta$, and their multiplication isomorphisms, with $R\to A$ flat finitely presented. The algebraic homothety node applies to $M$ and identifies its scalar map with an isomorphism. By the affine-realization node its sheafification is the scalar map of $K|_U$. By the unit law of the strong monoidal $m_0$ of step 1, $c\circ r(s_K)=s_{K|_U}$ for the scalar map $s_K$ of $K$, with $c$ the isomorphism of step 1 [lem-pc-open-restriction-evaluation-mate-is-iso]; so $r(s_K)$ is an isomorphism on every $U\in\mathcal B$. The cone of that scalar map has zero cohomology on this covering basis, hence its cohomology sheaves vanish, proving the asserted isomorphism globally. The same algebraic node and affine Hom comparison give $\operatorname{Hom}(K|_U,K|_U[i])=0$ for $i<0$.

source.place: Tag 0E2V, affine reduction to dualizing.tex Tag 0E2G.

proof.text: On a basis open retain the preceding notation. Algebraic uniqueness supplies an unmarked isomorphism $b:M\to N$. The multiplication isomorphism defined by $\theta$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(A[0],N_1)=H^0R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,N_1)$ with $A$, sending $\theta$ to $1$; the same holds for $\gamma$. Because $b_1$ is invertible, $b_1\gamma$ is also a basis, so $b_1\gamma=u\theta$ for a unique $u\in A^\times$. Set $a=u^{-1}b$. Linearity gives $a_1\gamma=\theta$. If $a'$ is another such isomorphism, the homothety node writes $a^{-1}a'=v\,\mathrm{id}_M$ uniquely with $v\in A^\times$. Its action on the basis $\gamma$ is trivial, so $v=1$ and $a'=a$. The affine comparison transfers this to exactly one class-preserving isomorphism $\alpha_U:K|_U\to L|_U$.

source.place: Tag 0E2W, first two paragraphs: affine existence followed by normalization by a unit.

proof.text: Apply the diagonal-class basis descent node to $\mathcal B$. Its multiplication hypothesis is the supplied-pair condition for $\eta$; step 2 gives negative self-Ext on every basis open and step 3 gives the unique class-preserving local isomorphism. Its conclusion gives the unique global isomorphism $\alpha$, with $(Lp_1^*\alpha)\xi=\eta$. Repeat steps 2--4 for each open restriction, whose supplied-pair condition was proved in step 1. For the empty open the module derived category is the zero category, so both the scalar map and the only map between the two restricted objects are isomorphisms, and class preservation is automatic.

source.place: Tag 0E2W, gluing paragraph; Tag 0E2X, open restrictions.

proof.text: If $f$ factors through an open $V\subset S$, the universal property identifies $X\times_VX$ with $X\times_SX$: two maps to $X$ have the same composite to $S$ exactly when their composites to $V$ agree, since an open immersion is a monomorphism. Under this identification the diagonal, first projection and both classes are identical. Moreover $f^{-1}\mathcal O_S$ equals the inverse image of $\mathcal O_V$, so the test modules and finite-Tor condition are identical. The pseudo-coherent condition is intrinsic to $X$. Hence precisely the same supplied-pair predicate and scalar map are obtained. Uniqueness from step 4 identifies the comparison isomorphisms for the two bases.

source.place: Tag 0E2X, first paragraph: V-perfect equals S-perfect and the two fibre products agree.
